[[File:Aes Sedai Ancient.jpg|right|250px|thumb|The Banner of Light]]{{quote|It was a banner of red, bearing a circle in the middle, split by a sinuous line. One half of the circle was black, the other was white.|[[Gambits]], ''[[The Gathering Storm]]''}}
{{dablink|For other uses of the word "light," see [[Light (disambiguation)|Light]].}}
'''The Banner of Light''' is the most commonly used banner by the [[Dragon Reborn]] and his forces. The banner's symbol is that of the ancient [[Aes Sedai (Age of Legends)|Aes Sedai]] before the [[Breaking]]. In the time period of the books, it is also called '''al'Thor's Banner'''.{{ref/book|7|1}}

The False Dragon [[Guaire Amalasan]] used a modified version of the Banner of Light during his conquests, with the only difference being that the background was blue instead of red.{{ref|{{bwb}}, Chapter 11}}

==Appearances==

*[[Dobraine]] is carrying the banner at the battle of Dumai's Wells.{{ref/book|6|55}}
*During the battle of Dumai's Wells, [[Mazrim Taim]] commands [[Jur Grady]] to raise the banner through the hole in the top of the protective shield created by the [[Asha'man]].{{ref/book|6|55}}
*On arrival in Cairhien after Dumai's Wells, it is flying from the towers of the city along with three other flags: The [[Dragon Banner]], flag of Cairhien and that of [[House Saighan]].{{ref/book|7|4}}
*It is flying from the towers of [[Caemlyn]]'s [[Inner City]] when [[Elayne Trakand]] returns to [[Andor]] in order to stake her claim to the [[Lion Throne]].{{ref/book|8|28}}
*Rand sends a copy of the banner to [[Tuon]] to request a meeting.

==Trivia==
[[File:Aes_Sedai_banner.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The Banner of Light on the original cover of The Path of Daggers. Note that the white should be pointing up and the black, down.]] The original cover of ''[[The Path of Daggers]]'' erroneously displays the disc on the banner with the left half coloured black and the right half coloured white, when in fact it should be the other way around, as the black half is supposed to resemble the [[Dragon's Fang]], while the white half is supposed to resemble the [[Flame of Tar Valon|Flame]]. However, some renditions of ''The Path of Daggers'' cover do display the disc in its correct form.
